To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) star formation rates depend strongly on the velocity field, and (2) star formation rates are consistent with Silk’s formula if the porosity of hot gas is taken into account.
the star formation rate depends most strongly on how the kinetic energy of the medium is maintained.

(i) star forming regions are preferentially found in the high-density regions of the ISM, (ii) the SFR is a strong function of the gas velocity dispersion, (iii) the SFR can be predicted to better than a few to a factor of a few by a simple model based on the hot gas porosities and the average gas densities of the ISM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between the physics of star formation and the structure and dynamics of the ISM, and the resulting SFR.
the physical processes which govern star formation in the ISM.
the physical mechanisms which control the SFR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SFR is a strong function of the velocity dispersion, and that the density and porosity of the ISM are secondary effects.
the star formation rate depends on the underlying velocity dispersion, the porosity of hot gas, and the average density of the ISM.

, in order to understand the local physics of star formation in the ISM, one needs to consider the full set of physics we have implemented here, including self-gravitational collapse, radiative cooling and supernovae energy input.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SFR is determined by the underlying turbulent flow.
the ISM is highly structured and its structure depends on the underlying physical processes.
, while the PDF of the gas density is sensitive to the physics of the ISM, the SFR is more sensitive to the gas velocity dispersion, and the hot gas porosities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the star formation rate is strongly affected by the underlying turbulence in the interstellar gas, and that the turbulence in the ISM is sustained by feedback processes which inject energy into the gas on a variety of scales.
the SFR is sensitive to the underlying velocity field and the hot gas porosities, and thus the SFR is a function of the local ISM physics and the local environment.
